name: Erdős–Straus conjecture
question: Can 4/n always be written as three positive unit fractions for every integer n at least two?
first_attack: Seek new modular covering identities and exact certificates
dispatch_next: Nine polynomial identities from the straus_identities mine now cover 106 of the 117 primes n <= 8000 with n = 1 (mod 24), including the primary progressions n = 120t+73 and n = 120t+97. The 11 uncovered primes all lie in {1, 49} (mod 120). Attack those two remaining classes with a non-Mordell idea, or name an explicit family outside the recorded progressions; do not extend the verified search range.
dispatch_why: Nine polynomial identities already cover 106 of 117 hard-class primes through 8,000. Extending the verified range stays inside published computations; the missing piece is a non-Mordell idea for the classes 1 and 49 mod 120.

campaign.method: Modular covering identities with unit-fraction certificates
campaign.hypothesis: For every integer n >= 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Find a polynomial identity family covering a residue class of primes not covered by the classical Mordell identities, and prove it symbolically.
campaign.next_experiment: Nine polynomial identities from the straus_identities mine now cover 106 of the 117 primes n <= 8000 with n = 1 (mod 24), including the primary progressions n = 120t+73 and n = 120t+97. The 11 uncovered primes all lie in {1, 49} (mod 120). Attack those two remaining classes with a non-Mordell idea, or name an explicit family outside the recorded progressions; do not extend the verified search range.
campaign.falsification: An n together with a proof that no positive-integer triple exists; a finite search failure is not a counterexample.
campaign.blocker: Classical identities leave quadratic-residue classes uncovered, and known results show identities of the standard polynomial type cannot cover them all; a different idea is needed.

probes.name: Erdős–Straus conjecture
probes.title: Erdos-Straus unit-fraction certificates for every n up to N
probes.frontier: Known: computational verification is reported far beyond this range (at least 10^14 in the literature). Reproduction only.

smoke.scope: For every integer 2 <= n <= 20,000, explicit positive integers x <= y <= z with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx).

deep.scope: For every integer 2 <= n <= 1,000,000, explicit positive integers x <= y <= z with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx).

milestones.title: Erdos-Straus triples certified for every 2 <= n <= 20,000
milestones.scope: Finite range only; known computational verification is far larger
milestones.description: Explicit (x, y, z) with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx) for all 19,999 integers, each re-checked by exact integer arithmetic; the deep run covers n <= 10^6.

milestones.title: Erdos-Straus residues for primes 1 mod 24 through 8,000
milestones.scope: Explicit solutions in a finite range; not an identity and not a proof
milestones.description: All 117 such primes have a checked solution whose residue 4x-n lies in {3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23}. The equation is rechecked without calling the search.

milestones.title: Parametric Erdos-Straus identities on nine hard-class progressions
milestones.scope: Polynomial identities on named arithmetic progressions; classical covering style, not a full proof
milestones.description: Nine closed forms, including n=120t+73 and n=120t+97, are proved as polynomial identities. Through 8,000 they cover 106 of 117 primes that are 1 mod 24; the 11 misses all lie in {1,49} mod 120.

formal_statement.encodes: 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z cleared to 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx) with x, y, z > 0.
not_encoded: A parametric solution for every residue class

kernel_checked.claim: Explicit positive solutions for every 2 ≤ n ≤ 100, re-checked by the kernel.
For every n with n % 4 = 3, positive denominators exist; n=4k+3 uses (k+1, 2n(k+1), 2n(k+1)), with no finite bound.
